proof.text: The dual of E is finite locally free by the source library Modules.IsFiniteLocallyFree.dual. Apply the single-image representability theorem to the reference E twice: first with F=E, then with F=E dual. This gives immersions j1:W1→S and j2:W2→S representing the two separate universal local rank conditions.

Let W be the fibre product W1×_S W2 and j its first projection followed by j1. The first projection is the base change of j2, so j is an immersion by Mathlib stability under base change and composition.

Unfold the universal common-rank predicate and project its witnesses to obtain each single-image condition. The converse is [lem-sc-picard-universal-rank-match-conjunction], which refines the independent neighbourhoods and identifies their ranks using E.

A factor through W gives factors through each Wi by composing with its projections. Conversely the two single-image conditions give maps a:T→W1 and b:T→W2 with a≫j1=g=b≫j2. Their pullback lift is a factor through j. These constructions prove the equivalence for every test g, including the empty scheme.
